data: PhysioNet slpdb slp01a, EEG (C4-A1), fs=250 Hz, 10-min segment (samples 600-1200 s)
convention: ARA = T_release/T_accumulation = median(decay)/median(rise) per base cycle; symmetric sine => 1.0 (ridge/pacemaker)
method: bycycle discipline (Cole & Voytek 2017): narrowband Butterworth bandpass LOCATES cycle boundaries (zero crossings); rise (trough->peak) and decay (peak->trough) measured on RAW signal between raw-refined extrema.
finding: All 5 EEG bands collapse from old >2 catalogue values to the ARA~1 ridge: order-unity, near-symmetric oscillators (point estimates 0.80-0.98, mild build-skew).
honesty_caveat: Sub-cycle asymmetry is METHOD-SENSITIVE. A harmonic-preserving variant pushes some bands slightly ABOVE 1 instead of below. What is ROBUST across methods: every band is order-unity and bounded (~1), definitively NOT >2. The precise side of the ridge (mild snap vs mild engine) is not robustly resolved from one record. Dylan correct: a rhythm DOES have build/release in its base cycle — here it is near-balanced.
